35/S0.subgoal: Describe the role of requirement gathering in the interactive system development life cycle as the stage where end-user usability requirements are identified.

35/S1.subgoal: Distinguish system-centered design from user-centered design by whose needs drive the design.

35/S2.subgoal: Identify end-user usability requirements as distinct from feasibility, interface design, and code design decisions using a calendar app example.

35/S3.subgoal: Explain usability requirements as non-functional interface-quality requirements relevant to interactive systems used by non-experts.

35/S4.subgoal: Describe the contextual inquiry method, including why requirement gathering must start from specified users and a specified context of use according to the ISO usability definition.

35/S5.subgoal: Explain why contextual inquiry is important for system development by showing how observed user activities determine essential features.

35/S6.subgoal: Summarize the main points of the lecture.

goal.goal: Explain the user-centered process of identifying and specifying usability requirements for an interactive system, from lifecycle positioning and requirement classification to contextual inquiry of specified users.
goal.achieves: Provides the learner with the foundational requirement-gathering skill needed to start the XR case study with user-centered usability requirements that guide later design and implementation.

objectives.goal: Frame requirement gathering as the user-centered stage of interactive system development where end-user usability requirements are identified.
objectives.achieves: Gives the learner a user-needs basis for beginning an XR system rather than starting from technical or system capabilities.

objectives.goal: Distinguish end-user usability requirements from feasibility, interface design, and code design decisions by characterizing them as non-functional interface-quality requirements for interactive systems used by non-experts.
objectives.achieves: Lets the learner focus requirement work on the usability issues that must be addressed before system design and implementation in the XR case study.

objectives.goal: Describe how contextual inquiry gathers usability requirements from specified users in a context of use and yields essential features from observed user activities.
objectives.achieves: Gives the learner a user-centered method for discovering the features and constraints that should drive design refinement in the XR case study.
